evaluationApproach.summary: The AI must evaluate Academy Director candidates on long-term player development, academy governance, technical standards, coach development, safeguarding, pathway design, staff collaboration and evidence of implementation. Do not substitute Head Coach or Director of Coaching criteria.
evaluationApproach.corePrinciple: Strong answers connect academy philosophy to observable age-appropriate development standards, coach support, reliable player progression measures and accountable organizational leadership.

mandatoryRules.rule: Score the response against the Academy Director role, not against Office Staff or another coaching position.
For questions requesting a real situation or example, do not award 4/4 unless the response includes the situation, the candidate's action and the outcome.
Distinguish between a generally positive statement and demonstrated competence.
Treat relevant but generic answers as acceptable or good, not automatically strong.
Flag contradictions between the written questionnaire and the video response.
Do not infer expertise, credentials or results that the candidate did not state.
Do not reduce scores because of accent, grammar, speaking speed, appearance, age, gender, ethnicity or disability. Evaluate content only, except when audio is impossible to assess.
Do not reward excessive confidence, length or technical vocabulary unless the content is relevant and accurate.

calibrationOverall.classification: Basic / acceptable; evidence or depth is limited
calibrationOverall.strongestAreas: Academy philosophy, coach collaboration, age-group alignment
calibrationOverall.mainWeaknesses: Safeguarding governance detail, longitudinal player metrics, coach quality assurance, 90-day implementation specificity
calibrationOverall.summary: The fictional candidate demonstrates a credible foundation in academy philosophy, age-group alignment and coach collaboration. However, many answers remain insufficiently detailed about quality-assurance systems, objective progression measures, safeguarding governance and implementation ownership. Request examples of an academy operating plan, coach reviews, player development evidence and first-90-day milestones.

questions.text: Can you describe your professional pathway and the experiences that prepared you to lead an academy?
questions.evaluates: Leadership preparation and relevant academy responsibility.
strong: Names roles, academy sizes and age groups.
Explains decisions owned, outcomes and lessons.
Distinguishes playing from management experience.
questions.acceptable: Relevant background but little detail on responsibility or results.
questions.weakOrConcerning: Relies on reputation or credentials without leadership evidence.

calibration.response: I led the U13-U17 program for four years, helped revise coach plans and chaired monthly reviews, although I have not managed the full academy budget.
calibration.label: Good
calibration.assessment: Relevant role-specific reasoning with some practical detail; stronger verification, outcomes or implementation evidence would be needed for 4/4.

questions.text: How would you define the mission of an academy director within a modern football organization?
questions.evaluates: Long-term mission, welfare and strategic alignment.
strong: Balances player development, education, safeguarding and pathway outcomes.
Aligns club identity and resources.
Defines measurable goals and governance.
questions.acceptable: Describes player development and club identity without operational measures.
questions.weakOrConcerning: Defines success only as winning or selling players.

calibration.response: The mission is to develop players and coaches, create a clear route through age groups and protect enjoyment and welfare, with progress reviewed every season.
calibration.label: Good
calibration.assessment: Relevant role-specific reasoning with some practical detail; stronger verification, outcomes or implementation evidence would be needed for 4/4.

questions.text: What leadership principles guide your decisions when managing a long-term development structure?
strong: Gives clear values, transparent decisions, consultation, safeguarding and conflict management.
Illustrates trade-offs with an example.
questions.acceptable: Names reasonable values but lacks a concrete decision process.
questions.weakOrConcerning: Favors short-term results or arbitrary authority.

calibration.response: I value fairness, communication and consistency. I consult coaches and explain difficult decisions, but I have not formalized an appeal process.
calibration.label: Acceptable
calibration.assessment: Demonstrates a plausible general approach but does not provide enough operational detail, evidence or follow-up to justify a higher score.

questions.text: How do you ensure technical and tactical standards are consistent across all age groups?
strong: Defines academy-wide principles, age-band objectives and shared language.
Uses observations, coach support and review without rigid uniform drills.
questions.acceptable: Has a shared curriculum but limited quality assurance.
questions.weakOrConcerning: Requires identical tactics and sessions for every age.

calibration.response: We use a progression matrix for receiving, scanning and team principles, and coaches discuss age-specific objectives each month.
calibration.label: Good
calibration.assessment: Relevant role-specific reasoning with some practical detail; stronger verification, outcomes or implementation evidence would be needed for 4/4.

questions.text: How do you evaluate whether training sessions meet development objectives?
questions.evaluates: Training quality assurance and learning evidence.
strong: Sets observable session objectives, observes practice, reviews player behavior and coach reflection.
Checks retention and match transfer.
questions.acceptable: Uses observation and feedback without repeatable indicators.
questions.weakOrConcerning: Judges sessions only by energy or drill completion.

calibration.response: I watch sessions, compare the practice with the weekly objective and give coaches feedback. I would like a more consistent follow-up form.
calibration.label: Acceptable
calibration.assessment: Demonstrates a plausible general approach but does not provide enough operational detail, evidence or follow-up to justify a higher score.

questions.text: What indicators do you use to measure real player progression?
strong: Uses individual baselines, technical/tactical behaviors, maturation context, retention, match transfer and regular review.
Avoids raw-result bias.
questions.acceptable: Lists several indicators without benchmarks or validity checks.
questions.weakOrConcerning: Equates progression with wins, goals or physical size.

calibration.response: We compare individual plans every term, use coach observations and video examples, and consider decision-making as well as physical changes.
calibration.label: Good
calibration.assessment: Relevant role-specific reasoning with some practical detail; stronger verification, outcomes or implementation evidence would be needed for 4/4.

questions.text: How do you design and implement a unified development philosophy across the academy?
questions.evaluates: Philosophy translated into a working operating model.
strong: Engages stakeholders, documents age-band principles, pilots implementation, trains coaches and audits adoption.
Revises with evidence.
questions.acceptable: States a clear philosophy but limited implementation plan.
questions.weakOrConcerning: Imposes slogans with no coach support or follow-up.

calibration.response: I would first agree on three or four core principles with staff, write age-group objectives and introduce monthly coaching meetings.
calibration.label: Good
calibration.assessment: Relevant role-specific reasoning with some practical detail; stronger verification, outcomes or implementation evidence would be needed for 4/4.

questions.text: How do you maintain consistency while allowing coaches freedom to express their coaching identity?
strong: Separates non-negotiable developmental principles from flexible methods.
Sets review criteria and constructive escalation.
questions.acceptable: Supports flexibility but does not define boundaries.
questions.weakOrConcerning: Demands identical sessions or allows contradictory practices.

calibration.response: I expect the same player-development outcomes, but coaches can choose exercises and feedback styles that fit their group.
calibration.label: Good
calibration.assessment: Relevant role-specific reasoning with some practical detail; stronger verification, outcomes or implementation evidence would be needed for 4/4.

questions.text: What principles guide your long-term player development model?
strong: Accounts for maturation, learning rates, opportunity, welfare, technical/tactical and psychosocial development.
Sets progression checkpoints.
questions.acceptable: Mentions long-term development but little differentiation.
questions.weakOrConcerning: Specializes early or excludes late developers solely on current performance.

calibration.response: We avoid judging players from one season, review their individual plans and consider late maturation before changing their pathway.
calibration.label: Good
calibration.assessment: Relevant role-specific reasoning with some practical detail; stronger verification, outcomes or implementation evidence would be needed for 4/4.

questions.text: How do you recruit, mentor, and evaluate academy coaches?
strong: Defines role criteria, structured interviews, safeguarding verification, observations, mentoring, documented reviews and fair feedback.
questions.acceptable: Describes recruitment and mentoring but no clear evaluation cycle.
questions.weakOrConcerning: Uses contacts alone or ignores safeguarding.

calibration.response: I interview for teaching ability, observe trial sessions and pair new coaches with experienced mentors; formal evaluation is twice a year.
calibration.label: Good
calibration.assessment: Relevant role-specific reasoning with some practical detail; stronger verification, outcomes or implementation evidence would be needed for 4/4.

questions.text: What tools or methods do you use to monitor coaching quality?
strong: Uses observation rubrics, session plans, player learning, coach reflection, stakeholder feedback and follow-up.
Avoids win-only measures.
questions.acceptable: Uses observation but lacks calibration or tracking.
questions.weakOrConcerning: Ranks coaches only by results or popularity.

calibration.response: I review plans and observe sessions, then discuss what players actually learned; I have not yet used a shared scoring rubric.
calibration.label: Acceptable
calibration.assessment: Demonstrates a plausible general approach but does not provide enough operational detail, evidence or follow-up to justify a higher score.

questions.text: How do you support coaches in their professional growth and licensing pathway?
strong: Creates individual development plans, mentoring, protected learning time, certification support and checks application in sessions.
questions.acceptable: Encourages courses and mentorship without follow-up.
questions.weakOrConcerning: Treats licenses as sufficient proof of competence.

calibration.response: We offer monthly workshops and help staff identify licensing options, then ask them to share one practical learning point.
calibration.label: Acceptable
calibration.assessment: Demonstrates a plausible general approach but does not provide enough operational detail, evidence or follow-up to justify a higher score.

questions.text: How do you structure player progression from grassroots to elite level?
strong: Defines age-appropriate milestones, selection reviews, multiple routes, late-development opportunities and transition support.
questions.acceptable: Describes age-group promotion but little evidence or inclusion.
questions.weakOrConcerning: Uses fixed early labels or guarantees professional outcomes.

calibration.response: We use age-group reviews and occasional training with older teams, while keeping options open for players who develop later.
calibration.label: Acceptable
calibration.assessment: Demonstrates a plausible general approach but does not provide enough operational detail, evidence or follow-up to justify a higher score.

questions.text: How do you integrate technical, tactical, physical, and mental development into one system?
strong: Coordinates staff around individual plans and workload.
Respects specialist expertise, welfare, confidentiality and measurable goals.
questions.acceptable: Names all dimensions but lacks integration processes.
questions.weakOrConcerning: Makes clinical claims or runs conflicting workloads.

calibration.response: Our technical and physical staff meet with coaches each term and align player priorities; mental support is referred to qualified professionals.
calibration.label: Good
calibration.assessment: Relevant role-specific reasoning with some practical detail; stronger verification, outcomes or implementation evidence would be needed for 4/4.

questions.text: How do you manage transitions between age groups and competitive levels?
questions.evaluates: Continuity and player welfare during transitions.
strong: Uses readiness evidence, handover notes, player/family communication, trial periods, support and follow-up.
questions.acceptable: Uses coach meetings and trials but limited structured monitoring.
questions.weakOrConcerning: Promotes solely by size or leaves players unsupported.

calibration.response: Coaches share development notes and invite selected players to train up before a move, with a review after several weeks.
calibration.label: Good
calibration.assessment: Relevant role-specific reasoning with some practical detail; stronger verification, outcomes or implementation evidence would be needed for 4/4.

questions.text: How do you collaborate with technical staff, performance departments, and club leadership?
strong: Defines decision rights, regular reporting, shared objectives, confidentiality and conflict resolution across departments.
questions.acceptable: Describes regular meetings without escalation or governance detail.
questions.weakOrConcerning: Works independently or shares private player data inappropriately.

calibration.response: I hold regular technical meetings and report priorities to club leadership; responsibilities are usually clear but not always documented.
calibration.label: Acceptable
calibration.assessment: Demonstrates a plausible general approach but does not provide enough operational detail, evidence or follow-up to justify a higher score.

questions.text: What metrics do you use to evaluate academy success beyond match results?
strong: Tracks player retention, progression, development-plan outcomes, coach growth, safeguarding, education and equitable access.
Checks context.
questions.acceptable: Uses progression and retention but limited attribution or benchmarks.

calibration.response: I track retention, player promotions and coach education, and would like better evidence of individual learning over multiple years.
calibration.label: Acceptable
calibration.assessment: Demonstrates a plausible general approach but does not provide enough operational detail, evidence or follow-up to justify a higher score.

questions.text: If appointed today, what would be your priorities during your first 90 days?
strong: Provides 30/60/90-day sequence: stakeholder audit, safeguarding and resource review, baseline measures, quick wins, governance and communication.
questions.acceptable: Offers sensible priorities but lacks timelines or owners.
questions.weakOrConcerning: Promises immediate overhaul without understanding context.

calibration.response: First I would meet staff and review the pathway, then observe sessions and identify two or three priorities before proposing changes.
calibration.label: Acceptable
calibration.assessment: Demonstrates a plausible general approach but does not provide enough operational detail, evidence or follow-up to justify a higher score.
